modelName: Where the money goes in a neighborhood ME — catalytic seed capital against every other flow
modelNote: Section 9 of the RCN Design Record. A value network in Verna Allee's notation (roles, not people; every arrow names its deliverable; solid = tangible, dashed = intangible). Money is amber. The one thick amber arrow is catalytic seed capital: it flows once, at launch, and departs. Every other amber arrow is a different kind of money and is deliberately drawn thinner so the difference is visible. The dotted red arrow is the flow the design refuses: operating subsidy in year three. Built 2026-09-11 by Marc Pierson and Claude for the Section 9 rewrite, from Sections 2, 6, 8 and 9. PROVENANCE: nothing here is measured; every arrow is asserted from the design record. Draw a real one from the first ME that runs. IAD LEVEL: operational — these are payoff flows inside one action situation; the rule that money must be catalytic is a collective-choice rule set in the Platform's charter and is not drawn here.

nodes.label: Seed capital is the only money that enters before value exists; everything else is paid after residents recognize what was created. Nothing here is measured — it is a structure to argue with.
nodes.note: Section 9: seed capital 'funds new work at its launch and departs when the new work has become self-sustaining or when it has failed.' Section 2, Principle Two: everyone is paid, and paid downstream of value received.

nodes.label: FUNDERS
nodes.note: Foundations, government grants, individual donors, the cooperative's reinvestment. Diversified on purpose: no single source may control which MEs get seeded (Section 9). They can decline to fund a neighborhood; they cannot write its scorecard.

props.basis: Section 9 — Recovery and reuse; Section 10 — anti-capture

nodes.label: PLATFORM
nodes.note: The Neighborhood-Catalyzing Industry Platform (WWHA's granting arm). Seeds and supports, does not run. Holds the seed pool and cycles it. Its actors are paid only after residents recognize value.

nodes.label: PLATFORM ACTORS
nodes.note: Conveners and mentors — Carl, Chris, Jerry, Brent. Compensation and reputation ride on the MEs they seed. Never a fixed salary (Principle Two).

nodes.label: SOLUTION ME
nodes.note: Forms around a scenario, charters with a VAM, does the work, settles, dissolves or continues. Receives seed capital once; everything else it receives is earned.

nodes.label: INSTITUTION
nodes.note: A school, clinic, agency. Commits separately from the people it lends, often loaning a manager's time with no money changing hands, betting on less waste and delay for itself.

nodes.label: ME MEMBERS
nodes.note: People participating as themselves — a CHW, a school nurse, a parent, a community leader. Paid through the ME under the VAM in whichever of the four currencies they agreed: fiat, time, gifts, reputation.

nodes.label: RESIDENTS
nodes.note: The people whose lives the scenario touches, and the neighbors they define. Their recognition, registered on their own scorecard, is what every settlement waits for.

nodes.label: SCENARIO + PORTFOLIOS
nodes.note: The FedWiki scenario repository and the SODOTO portfolios. Where a failed ME still pays: what was tried, what was learned, who can now do what. Marc's proposed second currency of return — skills that spread, parts of a scenario completed.

edges.label: diversified capital
edges.note: Several sources. If a share must fund non-catalytically (a cooperative's reinvestment), the proportion is fixed in advance and held to.

edges.label: CATALYTIC SEED CAPITAL (once, at launch)
edges.note: Sized to what the launch requires; gated (Haier's three thresholds adapted); departs whether the ME succeeds or fails.

edges.label: loaned staff time, data, a changed process
edges.note: Usually no money. The institution's return is less waste and delay for itself, and a seat in the VAM if it wants one.

edges.label: the scenario addressed — coordination, service, a new association or business
recognition on the neighborhood's scorecard
edges.note: The acceptance that completes the transaction. Nothing below settles until this arrives.

edges.label: fees or payments, where the work earns them
edges.note: Only some MEs have a money metabolism of their own. Section 9: those are the ones that can return capital.

edges.label: VAM share — after recognition, in four currencies
return-to-Platform share of the VAM, where revenue exists
edges.note: This is what lets seed capital cycle to the next ME.

edges.label: Platform actors' share — only after residents recognize value
reputation
edges.note: Marc: likely worth more to Platform actors than money.

edges.label: enriched scenario, portfolio entries, skills that spread
edges.note: Paid whether the ME succeeded or failed. A failed ME returns no money and still returns this.

edges.label: what the next ME starts from
operating subsidy in year three
edges.note: Drawn so that it is visible as the thing the Platform must not do. If this arrow appears in a real drawing, the ME was never catalyzable or has become a program the money props up.
